inputs.name: external_url
inputs.description: Address people reach GitLab by, such as "https://gitlab.example.com". GitLab builds its links and clone URLs from it, and bundled NGINX listens on its scheme and port.

inputs.name: gitlab_version
inputs.description: GitLab CE release to install, such as "19.5.3". Raising it upgrades GitLab in place. Follow GitLab's upgrade path: stop at each required release on the way.

inputs.name: root_password
inputs.description: Password GitLab gives root when it first sets up its database. Pass it at run time with -var or TF_VAR_root_password; it never reaches state or the plan. Changing it later doesn't change root's password.

inputs.name: letsencrypt
inputs.description: Have GitLab get and renew a Let's Encrypt certificate for an https external_url. Needs public DNS for its host name and port 80 open to the internet.

inputs.name: reverse_proxy
inputs.description: Set it when a proxy in front ends TLS: bundled NGINX then serves plain HTTP on listen_port, and trusts X-Forwarded-For from trusted_proxies, such as { trusted_proxies = ["10.0.0.5/32"] }.

inputs.name: extra_config
inputs.description: More gitlab.rb settings, as Ruby, added at the end of the file, such as "puma['worker_processes'] = 2".

inputs.name: min_memory_mb
inputs.description: Memory, in MiB, a host needs before the circuit configures it. GitLab asks for 8 GB at the least; an 8 GB host reports a little less.
